thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — inference-pool gp-infer-pool experiencing node flaps (NotReady) x4 in 5m, API error spike 503s, latency spike to 2.1s. Pager sent to oncall.
sarah (oncall): I'm on it. noticing 503 rate increased at 1976543180, tying to gp-infer-pool. Starting triage.
leo (runtime): saw a couple of GPU-serving pods crash with `OOMKilled` and some kubelet evictions earlier. Could be node-level kubelet restarts causing pod churn.
mike (infra): grabbing node list now.

mike (infra): ```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=gp-infer -o wide
NAME                    STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-12-45.ec2       NotReady   <none>   30d  v1.24.x
ip-10-0-16-88.ec2       Ready      <none>   30d  v1.24.x
ip-10-0-22-11.ec2       NotReady   <none>   30d  v1.24.x
ip-10-0-31-99.ec2       NotReady   <none>   30d  v1.24.x
``` 

mike (infra): `kubectl describe node ip-10-0-12-45.ec2` shows repeated kubelet restarts and docker/cri OOM warnings. journald shows `kubelet: panic: runtime error` followed by systemd killing kubelet.

leo (runtime): that matches the pod crash timeline — when kubelet restarts, the runtime restarts containers, GPU drivers fail to reattach fast enough => pods OOM or fail init. We saw `nvidia-smi` failing on host after kubelet restart.

sarah (oncall): Is this isolated to a subset of AZ? Any correlation with kernel/driver updates?

mike (infra): looks AZ-specific: two NotReady in us-east-1a, one in us-east-1c. No recent node AMI roll; maybe memory pressure + kubelet oom. Checking cloud events.

cj (se): Customer-facing: we have increased 503s for a small number of customers (alpha-beta test group). Which customers are impacted and what's the ETA for mitigation? Need quick blurb for support.

sarah (oncall): Short note for support: "We're observing transient NotReady nodes in the gp-infer-pool causing increased 503s and higher latency. Engineers are mitigating by draining affected nodes and shifting traffic to standby capacity. We'll update in 15m with impact scope." Copy/paste that.

leo (runtime): Mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain the 3 NotReady nodes 2) scale up warm standby nodes in autoscaling group + wait for them to pass health checks 3) route traffic to dedicated backup pool (cpu-fallback or smaller gpus) for critical customers 4) restart kubelet on affected hosts and collect logs for postmortem.

mike (infra): executing cordon/drain for the nodes we can still reach. If node is NotReady we might need `--force` drain for pods stuck.

mike (infra): ```
$ kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45.ec2
$ kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-45.ec2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
``` 

sarah (oncall): While draining, can we temporarily increase the routing weight to gp-infer-backup in the service router? ops-bot, can you bump traffic to backup pool?

ops-bot: Routing change queued: increasing gp-infer-backup weight from 5% -> 50% for 20m window. Will roll back after stable.

cj (se): For support: Customers A and B show ~80-95% success drop for their inference calls; non-critical customers see a smaller hit. Notifying cust A rep.

leo (runtime): On affected host logs (excerpt): ```
Feb 20 17:02:12 kubelet[1234]: runtime error: invalid memory address
Feb 20 17:02:12 systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=2/INVALIDARG
Feb 20 17:02:13 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 22345 (containerd) score 1000
``` Looks like a memory spike triggered OOM which cascaded into kubelet failures.

mike (infra): I've rebooted one host after restarting kubelet didn't stabilize; host came back Ready and pods are rescheduled successfully. Reboot seemed to clear the GPU driver state.
sarah (oncall): Good. How many nodes are remaining NotReady?

mike (infra): One still NotReady (ip-10-0-22-11.ec2). Draining failed due to kubelet unresponsive. I'll try `ssh` and restart container runtime + kubelet.

leo (runtime): Also create an emergency overlay that routes critical customers to model-variant-stable which runs on dedicated pool we control. That will reduce impact for top-tier customers.

cj (se): Customer comms: sending a short update to affected customers: "We’re mitigating an infrastructure-level issue causing transient errors; we have shifted traffic to standby capacity for critical workloads. We will follow up with root cause and ETA in 60m."

sarah (oncall): Action items captured:
- infra: stabilize remaining NotReady node (mike) — attempt container runtime restart, if not, reprovision host.
- runtime: collect kubelet/journald + nvidia-smi + dmesg logs (leo)
- oncall: maintain routing weight to backup and monitor 503/latency (sarah)
- support: customer comms and severity updates (cj)

mike (infra): Attempting remote fixes: ```
$ ssh ec2-user@ip-10-0-22-11
$ sudo systemctl restart docker && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
$ journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | tail -n 50
``` If that fails I'll request replacement via ASG.

leo (runtime): Collecting logs now; please capture `journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager`, `/var/log/syslog`, `dmesg | tail -n 200`, and `sudo nvidia-smi -q`.

sarah (oncall): Monitoring metrics: errors trending down after ops-bot reroute and node reboot. 503 rate for affected customers down from 18% -> 6% in last 6m. Latency back to 1.1s for majority.

ops-bot: Temporary routing change at 1976543315: gp-infer-backup weight increased to 50%.

mike (infra): Last node repair attempt failed; kernel OOM persists, provisioning replacement host now. ASG will spin new node in ~4m.

cj (se): Support update sent at 1976543399.

sarah (oncall): Preparing handoff to night oncall in 30m. I'll produce a short incident summary for next shift and set a ticket for postmortem.

sarah (oncall): Summary draft:
"At ~1976543180 we observed multiple nodes in gp-infer-pool enter NotReady due to kubelet crashes triggered by host memory pressure/OOM. This caused pod churn and GPU driver reattach failures leading to increased 503s and latency. Mitigations: cordon/drain affected nodes, rebooted one host, replaced one host via ASG, temporarily routed traffic to backup pool, and restarted kubelet/container runtime where possible. Impact reduced within 20m. Next steps: collect full logs, investigate memory sources (kernel vs process), evaluate kubelet memory limits, consider host-level OOM dials and kubelet restart backoff improvements. Postmortem ticket: INF-PRD-197654 (placeholder)."

leo (runtime): I'll attach logs to INF-PRD-197654 and include `nvidia` driver state, containerd stack traces, and pod resource usage leading up to OOM.

ops-bot: Routing rollback scheduled at 1976544435 unless incident extended.

mike (infra): New node in ASG registered at 1976543388 and passed kubelet health checks. gp-infer-pool size back to nominal.

sarah (oncall): Last check — 503 spike down to baseline, nodes stable. Handoff notes posted. I'm escalating for postmortem and adding infra/runtime to the RCA. Assigning to mike + leo.

cj (se): Thanks — I'll keep support looped and update customers when the RCA is available. Closing customer-facing incident note for now.

sarah (oncall): Handoff to night oncall @lee in 30m. Please refer to INF-PRD-197654 for details. If anything regresses, page oncall immediately.

ops-bot: Incident state: mitigated. Severity: Sev2. Time to mitigation: ~25m. Logs archived at https://redwood.internal/incident/INF-PRD-197654/logs

sarah (oncall): Good work team. Postmortem follow-up item list: host OOM tuning, kubelet backoff config, automated reroute playbook refinement, add a health-check gate for GPU driver readiness. I'll convert list to tasks after handoff.

mike (infra): +1. Will gather provisioning timeline and AMI metadata for RCA.

leo (runtime): +1. Will query serving runtime metrics for pre-OOM GPU memory usage and pod eviction history.

sarah (oncall): Handoff complete. Chat muted by oncall."
